---
title: Themes
description: Any Bootswatch theme, light and dark together, and your own CSS.
order: 7
---

smalldocs ships the 25 themes of [Bootswatch](https://bootswatch.com) 5.3, each as the plain CSS that
Bootswatch builds. Name one in `format.html.theme`:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: flatly
```

The themes: cerulean, cosmo (the default), cyborg, darkly, flatly, journal, litera, lumen, lux,
materia, minty, morph, pulse, quartz, sandstone, simplex, sketchy, slate, solar, spacelab,
superhero, united, vapor, yeti and zephyr. `bootstrap` gives Bootstrap with no theme.

## Light and dark

Give both, and the navbar or the sidebar gets a toggle. The reader's choice is kept in the browser.
This site does it:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: cosmo
      dark: darkly
```

## How the page follows the theme

Quarto compiles each theme's Sass with its own, so it needs a Sass compiler. smalldocs does not. A
Bootstrap 5.3 theme sets its colours, fonts and borders as CSS variables, such as `--bs-primary`,
`--bs-body-bg` and `--bs-border-color`. smalldocs' own stylesheet, which lays out the navbar, the
sidebar, the table of contents, callouts and listings, uses only those variables. So every part of
the page takes the theme's colours, in light and in dark.

## Your own CSS

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    css: styles.css
```

`styles.css` loads after the theme and after smalldocs' stylesheet. Set Bootstrap's variables to
change the theme, or smalldocs' own:

```css
:root {
  --bs-primary: #7a3e9d;     /* Bootstrap's colours */
  --sd-body-width: 900px;    /* the width of the text */
  --sd-sidebar-width: 280px; /* the width of the sidebar */
}
```

A `.scss` file in `theme` is not compiled; smalldocs says so when it builds.
